key_insight: Two-way coupling between superfluid vortex filaments and normal-fluid turbulence causes quantized vortices in superfluid $^4$He to roll up into coherent vortex bundles that mirror classical turbulent structures.
engineering_relevance: The result links superfluid turbulence to classical Kolmogorov scaling, offering a predictive multiscale framework for cryogenic flow modeling and heat-transfer applications.
method: Fully coupled vortex filament model + Navier--Stokes simulations
Resolved mutual friction between quantized vortices and the normal fluid
Tracked bundle formation, energy spectra, and time-scale ratios
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the coupled simulations reproduce a $k^{-5/3}$ spectrum and show bundle lifetime dependence on the ratio $t_\mathrm{cl}/\tau_\eta$ (with stability when $<20$).
watch_item: The conclusions rely on idealized spatially periodic turbulence and simulation-based coupling, so applicability to more complex geometries or experimental conditions may need validation.
paper_title: Two-Way Coupled Dynamics of Quantized Vortex Bundle Formation in Spatially Periodic Normal-Fluid Turbulence
